Documentation stack

Equipped to document at depth.

Built full organisational documentation — from scratch.

Took on the documentation gap every fast-moving team accumulates. Collaborated with cross-functional teams across engineering, product, and operations to capture, structure, and publish documentation people could actually find and trust.

Owned the full pipeline: expert interviews, information architecture, writing, review cycles, and Docusaurus deployment. Set up the repo, branching model, and contribution guide so team members could add to it without breaking structure.

Also set up a query-based knowledge base using Claude — team members ask a plain-language question and get a direct answer from internal docs. Significantly reduced the "where do I find X?" overhead.

About me

The hybrid translator your team is missing.

Most companies have engineers who can't explain what they built, and marketers who can't understand how it works. I grew up between both worlds.

ECE at Velammal Engineering College. Enterprise data pipelines at Wipro on Linux. Content engine at a B2B SaaS company. And now — full-cycle app development and process consulting.

I can read a technical brief and write the launch email for the same product on the same day. I know where automation breaks, where copy loses credibility, and where the documentation gap kills adoption.

Why this background is rare: Most content writers have never seen a production Linux terminal. Most engineers have never built a content calendar. Having done both means I write with real depth — and build systems with the user story already embedded.
